rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā is Meccan and has eleven verses, without disagreement.
rows.anchor: سورة الضحى مكية وآيها إحدى عشرة آية بلا خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the prior sūra promises that the most God-fearing will be spared, this sūra turns to God's favors upon the Prophet, the most God-fearing of all.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه فيما قبلها وسيجنبها الأتقى وكان سيد الأتقين رسول الله

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says the sūra about Abu Bakr is followed directly by the sūra about the Messenger, showing no intermediary between the Messenger and the Ṣiddīq.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام لما كانت الأولى سورة أبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه وهذه سورة رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says the ordering of Abu Bakr's sūra before the Prophet's does not prove Abu Bakr's superiority, citing the order of divine oaths and other examples of precedence without rank.
rows.anchor: وتقديم سورة الصديق على سورته عليه الصلاة والسلام لا يدل على أفضليته منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī dismisses the Imam's preceding analogy as a spring flower that cannot withstand close scrutiny.
rows.anchor: ثم أن ما ذكره زهرة ربيع لا تتحمل الفرك كما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-Ḍuḥā is the time when the sun rises above the horizon after appearing to observers, rather than sunlight or the sun's height; this better suits what follows.
rows.anchor: تقدم الكلام فيه والمراد به هنا وقت ارتفاع الشمس الذي يلي وقت بروزها للناظرين دون ضوئها وارتفاعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath singles out the day's youthful, strong period, whose force is far from its opposite; it is also called the sun's daily honor and good fortune.
rows.anchor: وتخصيصه بالأقسام به لأنه شباب النهار وقوله فيه قوة غير قريبة من ضدها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say this is the hour when God spoke to Moses and the magicians fell prostrate, making it apt for the assurance that God has not left the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولأنه على ما قالوا الساعة التي كلم الله تعالى فيها موسى عليه السلام وألقى فيه السحرة سجداً

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes al-Ḍuḥā to mean daytime generally, as in the verse about punishment coming upon a people at ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به النهار كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: An objection says the other verse contrasts ḍuḥā with night generally, whereas this passage contrasts it with night understood as intensely dark.
rows.anchor: واعترض بالفرق فإنه فوقع هناك في مقابلة البيات وهو مطلق الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response denies that the qualification necessarily means intensified darkness.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بمنع دلالة القيد على الاشتداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever the alternative, the apparent sense is the generic category of ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أن المراد الجنس أي وجنس الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse enumerates the great favors given from the Prophet's earliest life to revelation, using specific past favors to confirm future promises and reassure him; the clause is separated for this reason.
rows.anchor: طمأنينة وسروراً وانشراحاً وحبوراً ولذا فصلت الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza negates a negation and thereby affirms it in the strongest way, as though saying that God certainly found and sheltered him.
rows.anchor: والهمزة لإنكار النفي وتقرير النفي على أبلغ وجه كأنه قيل قد وجدك

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍī explains wajada as finding someone in a particular state; applied here to God, finding is figurative for knowledge through necessary association.
rows.anchor: ووجدته على ما قال الرضي بمعنى أصبته على صفة ويراد بالوجود فيه العلم مجازاً بعلاقة اللزوم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes sensory, inward-faculty, and intellectual kinds of finding; finding attributed to God means pure knowledge, since God has no organs or instruments.
rows.anchor: وفي مفردات الراغب لوجود اضرب وجود بالحواس الظاهرة ووجود بالقوى الباطنة ووجود بالعقل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take wajada as knowledge, with the pronoun as its first object and yatīman as its second.
rows.anchor: وقد فسره بعضهم هنا بالعلم وجعل مفعوله الأول الضمير ومفعوله الثاني يتيماً

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others take wajada as finding, transitive to one object, and parse yatīman as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم بالمصادفة وجعله متعدياً لواحد ويتيماً حالاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Literal discovery cannot apply to God because it would imply encountering something outside His knowledge and decree; the word must be figurative for His knowledge of it.
rows.anchor: أن المصادفة لا تصح في حقه تعالى لأنها ملاقاة ما لم يكن في علمه سبحانه وتقديره جل شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan is a child separated from his father before puberty; sheltering is joining one thing to another, so the verse means God sheltered the fatherless child through those who cared for him.
rows.anchor: واليتم انقطاع الصبي عن أبيه قبل بلوغه والإيواء ضم الشيء إلى آخر يقال آوى إليه فلاناً

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says ʿAbd Allāh died in Yathrib while the Prophet was a six-month fetus; after his birth his mother died when he was six, then his grandfather at eight, and Abū Ṭālib raised him under his father's charge.
rows.anchor: روي أن عبد المطلب بعث ابنه عبد الله أبا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يمتار تمراً من يثرب فتوفي

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf instead says the Prophet's mother died when he was eight, after which his uncle cared for him closely until his mission.
rows.anchor: فكفله عمه وكان شديد الاعتناء بأمره إلى أن بعثه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو طالب
rows.claim: Abū Ṭālib told al-ʿAbbās that the child kept his body covered, smelled like musk, sometimes vanished from his bed yet answered when called, invoked God at meals, and avoided lies, laughter, pagan customs, and children's games.
rows.anchor: قال يوماً لأخيه العباس ألا أخبرك عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بما رأيت منه فقال بلى

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unattributed poem says that even in the cradle he displayed the happiness of his grandfather and unmistakable signs of nobility.
rows.anchor: في المهد يعرب عن سعادة جده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says wet nurses had refused the orphan, but God sheltered him with a nurse who came to love and care for him after receiving blessing through his companionship.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى ألم يجدك يتيماً أبتك المراضع فآواك من مرضعة تحنو عليك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers the unusual reading that yatīm means a unique, peerless pearl: God found the Prophet unmatched among Quraysh and sheltered him.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير على ما قال الزمخشري أن يتيماً من قولهم درة يتيمة والمعنى ألم يجدك واحداً في قريش عديم النظير فآواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls the pearl interpretation bizarre and says it would more fittingly mean that God found him peerless in all creation and selected him.
rows.anchor: والأولى عليه أن يقال ألم يجدك واحداً عديم النظير في الخليقة لم يحو مثلك صدف إلا مكان فآواك إليه

rows.speaker: أبو الأشعث
rows.claim: Abū al-Ashʿath reads the verb in the triliteral form fa-awā; it can mean that God sheltered him or had mercy on him, with the cited poetic line illustrating awā lahu.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو الأشعث فأوى ثلاثياً فجوز أن يكون من أواه بمعنى آواه وأن يكون من أوى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated either with what the preceding rhetorical question implies or with the verb negated by lam, under the same negation.
rows.anchor: عطف على ما يقتضيه الإنكار السابق كما أشير إليه أو على المضارع المنفي بلم داخل في حكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The main interpretation is that the Prophet did not know the revealed laws that reason alone cannot discover; revelation then guided him to them and taught him what he had not known.
rows.anchor: فهدك إلى مناهجها في تضاعيف ما أوحى إليك من الكتاب المبين وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says most commentators hold this interpretation, and al-Zajjāj also chooses it.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا كما قال الواحدي أكثر المفسرين وهو اختيار الزجاج

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib relates that, during a dark night on the journey to Syria with Abū Ṭālib, Satan led the Prophet's camel off course; Gabriel drove Satan away and returned the camel to the caravan.
rows.anchor: روى سعيد بن المسيب أن صلى الله عليه وسلم سافر مع عمه أبي طالب إلى الشام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the verse alludes to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib's report about Satan diverting the Prophet on the Syrian journey and Gabriel restoring him to the caravan.
rows.anchor: فما في الآية إشارة إلى ذلك على ما قيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for a story in which the child Muhammad became lost in Mecca's ravines; Abū Jahl found him while returning from his flocks and brought him back to his grandfather, who was praying at the Kaʿba.
rows.anchor: وقيل إشارة إلى ما روي عن ابن عباس من أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم ضل وهو صغير عن جده في شعاب مكة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the same story, Abū Jahl's camel refused to move with Muhammad behind him but rose when he placed him in front; the camel supposedly asked how the leader could follow the follower.
rows.anchor: فكانت الناقة تقول يا أحمق هو الإمام فكيف يقوم خلف المقتدي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the Prophet was lost a second time; ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib circled the Kaʿba seven times, then a heavenly caller directed him and Waraqa to the child under a samar tree in Tihāma.
rows.anchor: وقيل ضل عليه الصلاة والسلام مرة أخرى وطلبوه فلم يجدوه فطاف عبد المطلب بالكعبة سبعاً

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further report says his wet nurse Ḥalīma lost him near Mecca's gate while returning him to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib after weaning.
rows.anchor: وقيل أضلته مرضعته حليمة عند باب مكة حين فطمته وجاءت به لترده على عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the verse as a literal childhood loss on a road is weak: such an event would not count among the divine favors being recounted here.
rows.anchor: وضعف حمل الآية على ذلك بأن مثله بالنسبة إلى ما تقدم لا يعد من نعم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes ḍāll as a lone tree in the desert and means that God found the Prophet alone, then guided people to him rather than leaving him isolated.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضال الشجرة المنفردة في البيداء ليس حولها شجر والمراد أما وجدك وحدك ليس معك أحد

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd reads the verse as the Prophet being perplexed about explaining the revealed Book, then being guided to its explanation, a reading close to the main interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال الجنيد قدس سره أي وجدك متحيراً في بيان الكتاب المنزل عليك فهداك لبيانه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some mystics say God found the Prophet unaware of his own worth and disclosed his great standing.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم وجدك غافلاً عن قدر نفسك فأطلعك على عظيم محلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A mystical reading says he lacked understanding of pure love, so God gave him the cup of nearness and affection and guided him to divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل وجدك ضالاً عن معنى محض المودة فسقاك كأساً من شراب القربة والمودة

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says the Prophet was unaware, in eternity, of God's love for him, and God then bestowed knowledge of Himself; this resembles the preceding mystical view.
rows.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه كنت ضالاً عن محبتي لك في الأزل فمننت عليك بمعرفتي

rows.speaker: الحريري
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarīrī says the Prophet was uncertain amid the subtleties of love's meanings and was guided to them.
rows.anchor: وقال الحريري أي وجدك متردداً في غوامض معاني المحبة فهداك لها

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān once dreamed the phrase omitted a possessive noun, meaning God found the Prophet's people astray and guided them through him.
rows.anchor: ورأى أبو حيان في منامه أن الكلام على حذف مضاف والمعنى ووجد رهطك ضالاً فهدى بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī dismisses Abū Ḥayyān's dream interpretation with a wry remark that it is evident even while awake.
rows.anchor: وهو كما ترى في يقظتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse follows the same pattern as the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: على نمط سابقه والعائل المفتقر من عال يعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary lexical sense of ʿāʾil is needy or poor, from a root meaning to be impoverished.
rows.anchor: والعائل المفتقر من عال يعيل عيلاً وعيلة وعيولاً ومعيلاً افتقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads the favor as material enrichment: trade profits from the Syrian journey with Maysara, Khadīja's gift of her considerable wealth after marriage, and the resources brought by Abū Bakr.
rows.anchor: أي وجدك عديم المقتنيات فأغناك بما حصل لك من ربح التجارة وذلك في سفره صلى الله عليه وسلم مع ميسرة إلى الشام

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr brought all his wealth to the Prophet; when asked what he had left for his family, he replied that he had left God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: فأتى به كله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام ما تركت لعيالك فقال تركت الله تعالى ورسوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some interpret the enrichment as spoils of war, but al-Ālūsī objects that this Meccan sūra preceded the post-migration spoils.
rows.anchor: وقيل بما أفاء عليك من الغنائم وفيه أن السورة مكية والغنائم إنما كانت بعد الهجرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God enriched the Prophet's heart, since true wealth is contentment and money cannot enrich someone who lacks it.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد فنعك وأغنى قلبك فإن غنى القلب هو الغنى وقد قيل من عدم القناعة لم يفده المال غنى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further mystical view says God made the Prophet self-sufficient from everything besides Him; this is a richness grounded in need of God.
rows.anchor: وقيل أغناك به عز وجل عما سواه وهذا الغنى بالافتقار إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith supplicates: O God, enrich me through need of You and do not make me needy through independence from You; no grading is given here.
rows.anchor: اللهم أغنني بالافتقار إليك ولا تفقرني بالاستغناء عنك

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unattributed poet says poverty in relation to God is pleasing because of love for Him.
rows.anchor: ويعجبني فقري إليك ولم يكن

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Ḥajar grades the widely circulated saying poverty is my pride, when interpreted as spiritual poverty, false and fabricated.
rows.anchor: وشاع حديث الفقر فخرى وحمل الفقر فيه على هذا المعنى وهو على ما قال ابن حجر باطل موضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī emphatically rejects the more blasphemous mystical saying that when poverty is complete, it is God, along with the attempts to explain it.
rows.anchor: وأشد منه وضعاً وبطلاناً ما يذكره بعض المتصوفة إذا تم الفقر فهو الله سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علواً كبيراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second lexical sense is someone with many dependents, from ʿāla yaʿūlu; the wording of Jarīr's verse can bear either sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل عائلاً أي ذا عيال من عال يعول عولاً وعيالة كثر عياله ويحتمل المعنيين قول جرير

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarīr's line about the poor dependent supports the second lexical sense of ʿāʾil, and that sense is clearer in his verse.
rows.anchor:
قول جرير
: الله نزل في الكتاب فريضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers needy over having dependents here, supported by Ibn Masʿūd's reading ʿadīman and the fact that the Prophet did not yet have dependents early in life.
rows.anchor: ورجح الأول في الآية بقراءة ابن مسعود عديماً وأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يكن ذا عيال في أول أمره

rows.speaker: اليماني
rows.claim: Al-Yamānī reads ʿāʾilan as ʿayilan, with a doubled kasra yāʾ, like sayyid.
rows.anchor: وقرأ اليماني عيلاً كسيد بشد الياء المكسورة

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn suggests orphan means lacking a teacher, lost means lacking knowledge, and having dependents means the religious community needing guidance; God enriched the Prophet with revelation. Al-Ālūsī finds this strained.
rows.anchor: وذكر عصام الدين في هذه الآيات أنه يحتمل أن يراد باليتيم فاقد المعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the proposed allegory of orphanhood, misguidance, and dependents as deficiencies of teaching and knowledge is plainly strained.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects of the three verbs are omitted because they are clear from context and to preserve the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول في الأفعال الثلاثة لظهور المراد مع رعاية الفواصل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the omitted objects signal expansive generosity: God sheltered, guided, and enriched the Prophet and those connected with him; al-Ālūsī objects that the following fa-clauses resist this.
rows.anchor: وقيل ليدل على سعة الكرم والمراد آواك وآوى لك وبك وهداك ولك وبك وأغناك ولك وبك وظاهر الفاء مع تلك الأفعال نأبى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān means the human species, including believer and unbeliever, rather than only the disbeliever; the valid exception in the following verse and the default connected sense support this.
rows.anchor: وأريد بالإنسان الجنس فهو شامل للمؤمن والكافر لا مخصوص بالثاني واستدل عليه بصحة الاستثناء وأن الأصل فيه الاتصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a circumstantial expression describing the human as being in the best constitution; taqwīm means God's act of correction and adjustment.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال من الإنسان أي كائناً في تقويم أحسن تقويم والتقويم التثقيف والتعديل وهو فعل الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafājī construes the phrase by supplying a noun such as uprightness or the one made upright, yielding the construct phrase the uprightness of the best form.
rows.anchor: وقال الخفاجي هو مؤول بمعنى القوام أو المقوم وفيه مضاف مقدر أي قوام أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing treats fī as extra and the following words as an absolute object, with its adjective standing in for the verbal noun: God shaped him with the best shaping.
rows.anchor: أو في زائدة وما بعدها في موضع المفعول المطلق وقد ناب فيه عن المصدر صفته والتقدير قومناه تقويماً أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best form includes the finest physical and inward qualities: upright stature, beauty, perception, sound intellect, and more.
rows.anchor: والمراد بذلك جعله على أحسن ما يكون صورة ومعنى فيشمل ماله من انتصاب القامة وحسن الصورة والإحساس وجودة العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is a comprehensive microcosm joining the seen and unseen, giving and receiving, and containing the wonders of creation and all that was and will be; a poem attributed to ʿAlī says the greater world is folded within him.
rows.anchor: مجمع مجرى الغيب والشهادة ومطلع نيري فلكي الإفادة والاستفادة والنسخة الجامعة لما في رسائل إخوان الصفا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A line attributed to ʿAlī says a person's cure and disease are within, and that although one imagines oneself a small body, the greater world is folded within.
rows.anchor: ونسب لعلي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human form recalls and points to divine attributes: God made the human knowing, willing, and powerful, and the saying to take on God's qualities answers the concern that such attributes are forbidden to servants.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى رسم فيه من الصفات ما تذكره صفاته عز وجل وتدله عليها فجعله عالماً مريداً قادراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As further evidence of human honor, God says He created Adam with His two hands and ordered the honored angels to prostrate to him.
rows.anchor: ويكفي في هذا الباب وهو القول الفصل إن الله تعالى خلقه بيديه وأمر سبحانه ملائكته عليهم السلام بالسجود له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source cites the report that God created Adam in His image, with another version saying in the image of the Merciful, and argues that the latter rules out taking the pronoun to refer to Adam.
rows.anchor: وجاء إن الله تعالى خلق آدم على صورته وفي رواية على صورة الرحمن وهي تأبى احتمال عود الضمير على آدم

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh al-Rāzī says that whoever knows himself knows his Lord; people call it a hadith, but al-Nawawī says it is not established as one.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ الرازي من عرف نفسه فقد عرف ربه والناس يزعمونه حديثاً وليس كما قال النووي بثابت

rows.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Aktham and some Hanafis reportedly ruled that a conditional divorce took effect when a husband said his wife would be divorced if she were not fairer than the moon, citing this verse; al-Ālūsī says the distinction is obvious.
rows.anchor: وعن يحيى بن أكثم وبعض الحنفية أنهما أفتيا من قال لزوجته إن لم تكوني أحسن من القمر فأنت طالق بعد وقوع الطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-ʿAlaq, also called Sūrat Iqraʾ, is Meccan by consensus; verse counts differ: twenty in the Ḥijāzī count, nineteen Iraqi, and eighteen Syrian.
rows.anchor: وتسمى سورة اقرأ لا خلاف في مكيتها وإنما الخلاف في عدد آيها ففي الحجازي عشرون آية وفي العراقي تسع عشرة وفي الشامي ثماني عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators disagree about which revelation came first; many say this sūra was first.
rows.anchor: وفي أنها أول نازل أولا فذهب كثير إلى أنها أول نازل

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports with a chain meeting the soundness criterion from Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī that Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī said Iqraʾ was the first sūra revealed to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رجاء العطاردي قال كان أبو موسى الأشعر يقرئنا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥākim and al-Bayhaqī authenticated a report from ʿĀʾisha giving the same account that Iqraʾ was first.
rows.anchor: أخرج الحاكم في المستدرك والبيهقي في الدلائل وصححاه عن عائشة نحوه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the first revelations were Iqraʾ bi-smi rabbik followed by Nūn wa-l-qalam.
rows.anchor: وأخرج غير واحد عن مجاهد قال أول ما نزل من القرآن اقرأ باسم ربك ثم ن والقلم

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: In a report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections, Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh answers that Yā ayyuhā al-muddaththir was first; he responds to those who cite Iqraʾ by narrating the Prophet's account.
rows.anchor: وروي الشيخان عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن قال سألت جابر بن عبد الله أي القرآن أنزل أولا قال يا أيها المدثر

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
rows.claim: A mursal report with trustworthy narrators, transmitted by al-Bayhaqī and al-Wāḥidī, supports the view that al-Fātiḥa came first.
rows.anchor: واحتج له بحديث مرسل رجاله ثقات أخرجه البيهقي في الدلائل والواحدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fātiḥa-first report could describe what was revealed after Iqraʾ and al-Muddaththir, and the reports supporting the other order are stronger.
rows.anchor: وأجيب عنه بأن ما فيه يحتمل أن يكون خبرا عما نزل بعد اقرأ ويا أيها المدثر مع أن غيره أقوى منه رواية

rows.speaker: جابر بن زيد
rows.claim: Jābir ibn Zayd gives this sequence: Iqraʾ, Nūn, al-Muzzammil, al-Muddaththir, then al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: وجزم جابر بن زيد بأن أول ما نزل اقرأ ثم ن ثم يا أيها المزمل ثم يا أيها المدثر ثم الفاتحة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Another view, supported by ʿĀʾisha's account of the beginning of revelation, says only the opening passage through mā lam yaʿlam came first at Ḥirāʾ, with the rest revealed later.
rows.anchor: وقيل أول ما نزل صدرها إلى ما لم يعلم في غار حراء ثم نزل آخرها بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In the beginning-of-revelation report, the angel squeezed the Prophet three times, then recited the opening verses through the command to teach what was not known; the report is transmitted by Aḥmad and both Ṣaḥīḥ compilers.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة في حديث بدء الوحي وفيه فأخذني فغطني الثالثة حتى بلغ مني الجهد ثم أرسلني فقال اقرأ باسم ربك

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The account says Waraqa soon died and revelation then paused.
rows.anchor: إلى أن قالت ثم لم ينشب ورفة أن توفي وفتر الوحي

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Relating the pause in revelation, Jābir says the angel appeared seated between heaven and earth; the Prophet returned frightened, and God then revealed al-Muddaththir.
rows.anchor: عن جابر ابن عبد الله الأنصاري قال وهو يحدث عن فترة الوحي فقال في حديثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about the interruption and renewed revelation shows why Jābir's report does not establish al-Muddaththir as first overall: it was first after the pause.
rows.anchor: ويعلم منه ضعف الاستدلال على كون سورة المدثر أول نازل من القرآن على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī's chosen view is that the opening of this sūra was the first Qurʾānic revelation overall, supported by ʿĀʾisha's especially sound report.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة الصحيح كما قال البعض وهو الذي اختاره إن صدر هذه السورة الكريمة هو أول ما أنزل من القرآن على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawī says mā in the Prophet's response mā anā bi-qāriʾ is a negation, which fits a first command; otherwise refusing to read after prior instruction would be a grave sin.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ما فيه نافية بل قال النووي هو الصواب وذلك إنما يتصور أولا وإلا لكان الامتناع من أشد المعاصي

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf reconciles Jābir's report by taking his claim to mean the first complete sūra, while al-Muddaththir was first after the interval.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف الوجه حمل قول جابر على السورة الكاملة

rows.speaker: صاحب شرح صحيح مسلم
rows.claim: The commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim says Iqraʾ was first absolutely and al-Muddaththir first after the pause; it calls the Fātiḥa-first view clearly invalid.
rows.anchor: وفي شرح صحيح مسلم الصواب أن أول ما نزل اقرأ أي مطلقا وأول ما نزل بعد فترة الوحي يا أيها المدثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of iqraʾ is omitted but understood from context as the Qurʾān being revealed; the verb is not intransitive.
rows.anchor: أي ما يوحى إليك من القرآن فالمفعول مقدر بقرينة المقام

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda takes the bāʾ as extra and the object of iqraʾ as bismi rabbik, yielding the meaning remember your Lord; al-Ālūsī rejects this.
rows.anchor: على الباء زائدة كما قال أبو عبيدة وزعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ is original and marks association; it attaches to iqraʾ or to an omitted circumstantial expression, so the command means begin or open by God's name.
rows.anchor: بل هي أصلية ومعناها الملابسة وهي متعلقة بما عندها أو بمحذوف وقع حالاً

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Qatāda takes the bāʾ phrase as an omitted circumstantial expression: read while beginning with your Lord's name.
rows.anchor: وقع حالاً كما روى عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading one must begin by saying in God's name; opening with another name would not fulfill the command.
rows.anchor: ثم اقرأ وهو ظاهر في أنه لو افتتح بغير اسمه عز وجل لم يكن ممتثلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some use the command to argue that the basmala is part of every sūra, though al-Ālūsī says the inference needs discussion.
rows.anchor: واستدل بذلك على أن البسملة جزء من كل سورة وفيه بحث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others infer from the contrast that the basmala is not Qurʾān, but one can answer that the understood Qurʾān as object is restricted to what follows the basmala.
rows.anchor: وكذا الاستدلال به على أنها ليس من القرآن للمقابلة إذ لقائل أن يقول إنها تخصص القرآن المقدر مفعولاً بغيرها

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawī notes an argument that the basmala is not Qurʾān at the start of sūras because sound reports about the first revelation do not mention it.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم استدل على أنها ليست بقرآن في أوائل السور بأنها لم تذكر فيما صح من أخبار بدء الوحي

rows.speaker: المثبتون
rows.claim: Those who affirm the basmala as Qurʾān answer that it did not descend first but at another time, as other portions of the sūra also did.
rows.anchor: وجواب المثبتين أنها لم تنزل أولاً بل نزلت في وقت آخر كما نزل باقي السورة كذلك

rows.speaker: عكرمة والحسن
rows.claim: A report from ʿIkrima and al-Ḥasan says the first Qurʾānic revelation was bismi Allāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm, followed by the opening of Iqraʾ.
rows.anchor: خلاف ما أخرج الواحدي عن عكرمة والحسن أنهما قالا أول ما نزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk's report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Gabriel first instructed the Prophet to seek refuge, then to say the basmala.
rows.anchor: وكذا خلاف ما أخرجه ابن جرير وغيره من طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس أنه قال أول ما نزل جبريل عليه السلام على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يا محمد استعذ ثم قل

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says the basmala-first claim is not an independent view because the basmala necessarily descended with the sūra, making it the first verse overall; al-Ālūsī calls this reasoning plainly objectionable.
rows.anchor: وقال الجلال السيوطي أن هذا القول لا يعد عندي قولاً برأسه فإنه من ضرورة نزول السورة نزول البسملة معها فهي أول آية نزلت على الإطلاق وفيه منع ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ can also mean seeking assistance, but association is preferable because it avoids making God's name an instrument for something else.
rows.anchor: وجوز كون الباء للاستعانة متعلقة بما عندها أو بمحذوف وقع حالاً ورجحت الملابسة بلاسمتها عن إيها كون اسمه تعالى آلة لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command does not impose an impossible task: the Prophet knows that whatever is revealed as Qurʾān is what he is commanded to recite, and the command can include its own wording.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه ليس في الأمر المذكور تكليف بما لا يطاق سواء دل الأمر على الفور أم لا لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم علم أن ما أوحي قرآن فهو المكلف بقراءته

rows.speaker: الآمدي
rows.claim: Al-Āmidī uses the repeated command and question in the beginning-of-revelation report as evidence that clarification may be delayed: Gabriel says read three times before specifying what to read.
rows.anchor: قال الآمدي عند ذكر أدلة جواز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says Gabriel came to the Prophet at Ḥirāʾ with silk brocade bearing the opening verses; he asked him to read, and the Prophet replied that he could not read.
rows.anchor: وأما بناء الاستدلال على ما في بعض الآثار من أن جبريل عليه السلام جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī questions using the brocade account to explain the command as a recitation of visible writing, and notes that al-Āmidī's handling of the report also has a problem.
rows.anchor: وإن كان مشاهداً منزلة المجمل الغير المعلوم فلا يخفى حاله فتأمل ثم أن في كلام الآمدي من حيث رواية الخبر ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Prophet's Lord evokes nurturing and gradual development toward fitting perfection; the possessive pronoun signals that revelation brings him to the highest human completion.
rows.anchor: التعرض لعنوان الربوبية المنبئة عن التربية والتبليغ إلى الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description recalls God's first favor to the Prophet and signals God's power to teach him to read in the gentlest way.
rows.anchor: لتذكيره عليه الصلاة والسلام أول النعماء الفائضة عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم منه سبحانه مع ما في ذلك من التنبيه على قدرته تعالى على تعليم القراءة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the creator description confirms that the intended Lord is God, since Arabs called idols lords but did not attribute creation to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل لتأكيد عدم إرادة غيره تعالى من الرب فإن العرب كانت تسمى الأصنام أرباباً لكنهم لا ينسبون الخلق إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaqa can be intransitive, meaning the one who creates, or have a general omitted object, meaning the one who created everything; either way its force is universal.
rows.anchor: والفعل إما منزل منزلة اللازم أي الذي له الخلق أو مقدر مفعوله عاماً أي الذي خلق كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author raises, without yet answering in this passage, why humanity is singled out in the next verse if the creation description already has universal force.
rows.anchor: فعلى الوجهين يكون وجه تخصيص الإنسان بالذكر
